comments.text:
That is very outdated information. The pattern is quite clear: Greece experienced a massive negative net migration balance from 2011 to 2017. From 2018 onwards, the figure initially turned slightly positive, despite a brief, pandemic-related dip in 2020–21. Since 2022, the balance has been significantly positive again.

Between 2022 and 2025 alone, there was a net increase of around 138,000 people; 2023 and 2024 saw particularly strong figures. Specifically, the ELSTAT data for 2024 show 132,149 arrivals versus 78,014 departures, resulting in a net gain of 54,135.

greece has the biggest doctors per capita metric in all of Europe, this means that they have fewer opportunities here, it is even worse for engineers since there are lots of universities and no heavy industry, so yes, most people with degrees have big incentives to leave the country

I still think this is kind of a betrayal to the country that funds our education, even if universities are underfunded what is the purpose of exporting scientists without getting anything back? They come back every summer and spend some money but that is not the same help to the economy.

In my opinion Greeks shoot get free education but should be taxed based on their salary if they leave the country, this is at least until they cover their studies cost. I don't think this is unfair or unrealistic.
